subject: society
topic: Very long working weeks are linked to stroke
angle: Working long hours is linked to an increased risk of stroke and atrial fibrillation, as well as various other adverse health outcomes.
title: The cost of the long week

hooks.text: What is the cost of the extra hour?
You think you are productive. The evidence shows you are at risk.
You are trading your health for your output.
The blue light remains when the office is empty.

reveal.headline: Long hours increase your risk of stroke.
reveal.body: Research shows that working long hours is linked to a higher risk of stroke and atrial fibrillation. This extends to broader occupational health issues.

explain.headline: The physical cost of your hours.
explain.body: Long working hours are linked to circulatory disease, metabolic syndrome, and sleep conditions. The evidence shows these are connected to your overall health.

matters.headline: Your schedule is a health metric.
matters.body: That may be why your body feels different after a long week. Your work schedule is not just a time commitment. It is a physiological factor.

example.headline: The glow of the screen.
example.body: You sit at your desk at 9 p.m. The light from the monitor is the only thing in the room. Your coffee is cold. You are still typing.

question.headline: What is the cost of the extra hour?

stat.label: increased risk of stroke from long working hours

claims.text: Employees who work long hours have a higher risk of stroke than those working standard hours.
claims.quote: Employees who work long hours have a higher risk of stroke than those working standard hours; the association with coronary heart disease is weaker.

claims.text: Long working hours are linked to a 1.21-fold (95% CI 1.01-1.45) increased risk of stroke.
claims.quote: Our meta-analytic update of summary evidence suggests a 1.12-fold (95% CI 1.03-1.21) increased risk associated with coronary heart disease and a 1.21-fold (95% CI 1.01-1.45) increased risk of stroke

claims.text: Long working hours are linked to an overall odds ratio of 1.245 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.195-1.298) for occupational health.
claims.quote: The overall odds ratio between long working hours and occupational health was 1.245 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.195-1.298).

claims.text: Long working hours are linked to significant adverse effects on all-cause mortality, circulatory disease, diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, depressive state, anxiety, other psychological disorders, sleep condition, cognitive function, and health-related behavior.
claims.quote: Long working hours had significant adverse effects on most health outcomes.

verdict: The evidence consistently links long working hours to increased risks of stroke, atrial fibrillation, and broader occupational health issues.
caveat: The evidence for cardiovascular risk is described as somewhat inconsistent, with some studies showing a small risk and others showing larger effects.
caption:
Long working hours are linked to significant health risks. 

Studies link these hours to increased risks of stroke and atrial fibrillation, though cardiovascular risk data is somewhat inconsistent. Other links include metabolic syndrome, sleep conditions, and anxiety. 

How many hours did you work today?
